overview.intro:
Chapter 41 covers raw hides and skins (other than furskins) and leather: raw cattle, horse, sheep, goat, pig and reptile skins (4101–4103), tanned and crust leather such as wet-blue (4104–4106), finished leather (4107, 4112, 4113), chamois, patent and metallized leather (4114) and composition leather and leather waste (4115). Its **176 tariff lines** carry low base rates: 44 are Free and the rest pay 1.6% to 5%.

The extra duties by country matter more. Since **July 24, 2026** the Section 301 tariffs on 60 economies (10% or 12.5%, or a 10% floor for EU goods) reach **172 of the 176 lines**; only reptile leather (4113.30) and leather of other animals (4113.90) are on the U.S. note 52(b) exemption list. Brazil pays a separate 25% on top (37.5% on most lines). China pays 12.5% plus its 2018–2019 Section 301 duty of 25% (finished and tanned leather) or 7.5% (raw hides). **Japanese bovine and equine leather has paid 40% more since 1986** (9903.41.05), and goat and sheep leather too when dyed, colored, stamped or embossed. Since **August 22, 2026** goods of **Canada** pay a **50% Section 338 duty**, now on **14 lines** (mostly raw hides), even with a USMCA claim. The 2025 IEEPA tariffs ended on February 24, 2026. The U.S. imported **$450.5M** of Chapter 41 goods in 2025, 82% of it finished bovine leather (4107).

productGroups.label: Raw hides and skins of bovine (including buffalo) or…
productGroups.blurb: Raw cattle, buffalo and horse hides. Hides that are not pretanned are Free; most pretanned hides pay 2.4% to 5%. Canadian hides that are not pretanned (4101.20.10, 4101.50.10, 4101.90.10) and some pretanned lines pay the 50% Section 338 duty even with a USMCA claim. Untanned hides must meet USDA APHIS entry rules (9 CFR 95.16).

productGroups.label: Raw skins of sheep or lambs (fresh, or salted, dried…
productGroups.blurb: Raw sheep and lamb skins, with or without wool, are Free except pretanned skins in 4102.10.30 and 4102.29.30 (2%). Raw sheepskins with the wool on stay here (note 1(c)); Astrakhan, Caracul, Persian and similar lambskins go to Chapter 43 as furskins.

productGroups.label: Other raw hides and skins (fresh, or salted, dried, limed…
productGroups.blurb: Other raw skins: reptiles (4103.20), swine (4103.30), goats and kids, deer and other animals (4103.90). Raw skins that are not pretanned are Free. Reptile and deer skins are wildlife: they need an FWS declaration and, for CITES species, CITES permits.

productGroups.label: Tanned or crust hides and skins of bovine (including…
productGroups.blurb: Tanned (wet-blue) and crust cattle, buffalo and horse hides, not further prepared: Free to 5%. Japanese goods of this heading pay 40% more (9903.41.05). Five 4104 lines (4104.11.20, 4104.41.50, 4104.49.10, 4104.49.50) are exempt from Brazil's 25% Section 301 duty.

productGroups.label: Tanned or crust skins of sheep or lambs, without wool on…
productGroups.blurb: Tanned and crust sheep and lamb skins pay 2%. Nigeria supplied most of the $1.9M imported in 2025. Japanese skins of this heading pay 40% more if dyed, colored, stamped or embossed.

productGroups.label: Tanned or crust skins of other animals, without wool or…
productGroups.blurb: Tanned and crust goat (2.4%), swine (4.2%), reptile (Free) and other skins (3.3%). Reptile skins need CITES and FWS clearance; crocodilian skins must carry CITES tags.

productGroups.label: Leather further prepared after tanning or crusting…
productGroups.blurb: Finished cattle, buffalo and horse leather: 82% of Chapter 41 imports in 2025. Rates run from Free (upper and lining leather of up to 28 sq ft) to 5%; upholstery leather is 2.8%. Italian leather pays a flat 10%, Brazilian 37.5% plus the base rate, and Mexican is Free with USMCA. Japanese finished bovine leather pays 52.5%.

productGroups.label: Leather further prepared after tanning or crusting…
productGroups.blurb: Finished sheep and lamb leather pays 2% (fancy or not). Italy, Türkiye and France are the main suppliers. Japanese leather of this heading pays 40% more if dyed, colored, stamped or embossed.

productGroups.label: Leather further prepared after tanning or crusting…
productGroups.blurb: Finished goat and kid leather (2.4% or 2.8%), pigskin (4.2%), reptile leather (Free) and leather of other animals (3.3% or 1.6%). Reptile and other-animal leather (4113.30, 4113.90) is exempt from the 2026 Section 301 duties of every country, but not from Brazil's 25% or China's 25%.

productGroups.label: Chamois (including combination chamois) leather
productGroups.blurb: Chamois leather (3.2%), patent leather (2.3%) and patent laminated or metallized leather (3.6% for calf and kip, 1.6% other). Patent-look plastic or PU sheeting is not leather and is classified outside Chapter 41.

productGroups.label: Composition leather with a basis of leather or leather…
productGroups.blurb: Composition (bonded) leather with a basis of leather or leather fiber, and leather parings, waste, dust and powder not suitable for making leather articles: both Free. Parings of raw hides are not here (heading 0511).

workedExamples.title: Finished cowhide from Italy
workedExamples.body: Grain-split upper leather has a 3.3% base rate. EU goods pay the higher of the base rate or 10% (9903.05.39), so a $100,000 shipment pays **$10,000**. Italy supplied $155M of the $371M of finished bovine leather (4107) the U.S. imported in 2025.

workedExamples.title: Finished leather from Brazil
workedExamples.body: Brazilian goods pay the 3.3% base rate + 25% (9903.05.01) + 12.5% (9903.05.27) = 40.8%: **$40,800** on a $100,000 shipment. Whole-hide leather of up to 28 sq ft that is not fancy (4107.12.20.00, 2.4%) is on Brazil's exemption list (U.S. note 50(a)(ii)), so it pays 2.4% + 12.5% = 14.9%: **$14,900**.

workedExamples.title: Finished bovine leather from Japan
workedExamples.body: Japanese goods pay 12.5% in place of the 3.3% base rate (9903.05.49) plus the 1986 Section 301 duty of 40% (9903.41.05), which U.S. note 3 makes cumulative: 52.5%, or **$52,500** on $100,000. Goat or sheep leather from Japan pays the 40% only when dyed, colored, stamped or embossed: 12.5% if not, 52.5% if so.

workedExamples.title: Raw cattle hides from Canada
workedExamples.body: Whole raw hides over 16 kg that are not pretanned are Free at the base rate. Since September 15, 2026 the line is on the Section 338 list in U.S. note 51(b)(1), and the 50% duty (9903.03.12) applies even with a USMCA claim: **$50,000** on $100,000, or $60,000 without the claim (50% + 10% Section 301). Pretanned 'other' hides such as 4101.50.30 are not on the list and are Free with USMCA.

workedExamples.title: Crocodile or python leather
workedExamples.body: Reptile leather is Free and on the U.S. note 52(b) exemption list (9903.05.86), so from Italy, Singapore or Thailand it pays **$0** on a $100,000 shipment. From China it pays 25% (List 3, 9903.88.03) and from Brazil 25% (9903.05.01), because note 52(b) does not lift those. Each shipment needs CITES documents and an FWS declaration, and crocodilian skins must carry CITES tags (50 CFR 23.70).

notes.chapterNotes:
**Note 1.** This chapter does not cover: (a) parings or similar waste of raw hides or skins (heading 0511); (b) birdskins or parts of birdskins, with their feathers or down, of heading 0505 or 6701; or (c) hides or skins with the hair or wool on, raw, tanned or dressed (Chapter 43). Raw hides and skins with the hair or wool on stay in Chapter 41 when they are of bovine animals (including buffalo), equine animals, sheep or lambs (except Astrakhan, Broadtail, Caracul, Persian or similar lambs, and Indian, Chinese, Mongolian or Tibetan lambs), goats or kids (except Yemen, Mongolian or Tibetan goats and kids), swine (including peccary), chamois, gazelle, camels (including dromedaries), reindeer, elk, deer, roebucks or dogs.

**Note 2.** (a) Headings 4104 to 4106 do not cover hides and skins that have undergone a reversible tanning (including pre-tanning) process; they go in headings 4101 to 4103. (b) For headings 4104 to 4106, "crust" includes hides and skins that have been retanned, colored or fat-liquored (stuffed) before drying.

**Note 3.** Throughout the tariff schedule, "composition leather" means only substances of the kind in heading 4115.

seo.shortDescription: What changed for U.S. tariffs on raw hides and leather (HTS Chapter 41) since January 2025: the IEEPA tariffs and their end, the Section 122 surcharge, the 2026 Section 301 duties on 60 economies and Brazil, Canada's 50% Section 338 duty on raw hides and the 1986 Japan leather duty that still applies, with Federal Register citations.

tariffUpdates.intro:
This page compares two editions of the tariff schedule: the **2025 Basic Edition**, in force at the start of 2025, and the current **2026 Revision 21** (in force October 9, 2026). **No Chapter 41 base rate or line changed** between them: all 176 lines carry the same rate.

The changes were all extra duties by country. In 2025 Chapter 41 goods paid the IEEPA tariffs: the reciprocal tariff (10%, a country rate or a 15% floor for EU and Japanese goods), 40% more on Brazil, and 25%–35% on non-USMCA goods of Canada and Mexico. The IEEPA tariffs **ended on February 24, 2026** and a 10% Section 122 surcharge ran until July 23, 2026. Since **July 24, 2026** the Section 301 tariffs on 60 economies (10% or 12.5%) reach 172 of the 176 lines, and Brazil's own 25% applies from July 22. Since **August 22, 2026** Canada pays a **50% Section 338 duty**, now on 14 lines, USMCA or not. China's 2018–2019 Section 301 duties (25% or 7.5%) and **Japan's 1986 Section 301 duty of 40%** on its leather continue.
tariffUpdates.scope: Measures that reach Chapter 41 from any country: the 2026 Section 301 tariffs on 60 economies and on Brazil, the China Section 301 Lists 3 and 4A, the 1986 Section 301 duty on leather from Japan (9903.41.05), Canada's Section 338 duty, the Nicaragua Section 301 duty scheduled for 2027, and the 2025–2026 IEEPA and Section 122 duties that have ended. No antidumping or countervailing duty order covers a Chapter 41 product: the countervailing duty order on leather from Argentina (1990) was revoked in 1997. No Chapter 41 line is on the Section 232 auto-parts list (U.S. note 33(g)). For the rate each supplier pays, see Rates by country.

changes.title: No Chapter 41 base-rate changes
changes.detail: All 176 Chapter 41 lines carry the same general rate and the same statistical suffix in the 2026 Revision 21 as in the 2025 Basic Edition. No line was added, removed or renumbered.

changes.title: China Section 301 Lists 3 and 4A continue
changes.detail: USTR announced that the China Section 301 actions continue during the four-year review. For Chapter 41 this keeps +25% (9903.88.03) on 130 lines of tanned and finished leather and +7.5% (9903.88.15) on 45 lines of raw hides and leather parings from China.

changes.title: Canada Section 338 list widened to 14 Chapter 41 lines
changes.detail: Proclamation 11064 added bovine and equine hides that are not pretanned (4101.50.10, 4101.90.10) and full-grain upholstery leather (4107.11.50) to the 9903.03.12 list (U.S. note 51(b)(1)): 8 more lines at 50%, even with a USMCA claim. Proclamation 11065 changed the 9903.03.14 list but no Chapter 41 line.

changes.title: 50% Section 338 duty on 6 Chapter 41 lines from Canada
changes.detail: Proclamations 11046 (9903.03.12), 11047 (9903.03.13) and 11048 (9903.03.14), signed July 20, 2026, added 50% on listed products of Canada; Proclamation 11056 moved the start to August 22. The 9903.03.14 list (U.S. note 51(b)(3)) names raw bovine and equine hides 4101.20.10, 4101.20.20, 4101.50.20 and 4101.90.50 and pretanned reptile skins 4103.20.30. The duty applies even to USMCA-qualifying goods.

changes.title: Section 301 tariffs on 60 economies; reptile and other-animal leather exempt
changes.detail: 10% or 12.5% on all products of 60 economies (9903.05.20–9903.05.84), including Canada, China, Brazil, Mexico, the UK, Argentina, South Africa and India; EU goods pay at least 10% and Japanese goods at least 12.5% in place of the base rate. U.S. note 52(b) (9903.05.86) exempts reptile leather (4113.30) and leather of other animals (4113.90); the note 52(j) country lists name no Chapter 41 line. USMCA-qualifying goods from Canada and Mexico are exempt (9903.05.93, 9903.05.94).

changes.title: Section 122 import surcharge expired
changes.detail: The 150-day surcharge (9903.03.01) expired at the close of July 23, 2026.

changes.title: 25% Section 301 tariff on products of Brazil
changes.detail: USTR imposed 25% on all products of Brazil (9903.05.01). Its exemption list (U.S. note 50(a)(ii), 9903.05.03) names 7 bovine leather lines in Chapter 41: 4104.11.20, 4104.41.50, 4104.49.10, 4104.49.50, 4107.11.20 and 4107.12.20. From July 24 Brazil also pays the 12.5% forced-labor duty (9903.05.27) on 172 lines.

changes.title: USMCA joint review: not renewed, still in force
changes.detail: The United States did not agree to renew the USMCA in its current form. USTR said the Agreement remains in force pending resolution of the issues or until termination, so USMCA claims (SPI S) still apply.

changes.title: Section 122 surcharge replaces the IEEPA tariffs
changes.detail: 10% on products of all countries (9903.03.01) until July 23, 2026, on top of the base rate. No Chapter 41 line was on its exemption list (9903.03.03). USMCA-qualifying goods from Canada and Mexico were exempt. Japan's 1986 leather duty continued alongside it.

changes.title: All IEEPA tariffs end
changes.detail: After the Supreme Court held on February 20, 2026 (Learning Resources, Inc. v. Trump) that IEEPA does not authorize tariffs, Executive Order 14389 ended the Canada, Mexico, China, Brazil and reciprocal duties, and CBP stopped collecting them for goods entered from 12:00 a.m. ET on February 24. The 9903.01.xx and 9903.02.xx headings are still printed in Revision 21 but are no longer in effect. The 1986 Japan leather duty is a Section 301 duty, not an IEEPA duty, and was not affected.

changes.title: India's extra 25% IEEPA duty removed
changes.detail: Executive Order 14384 ended the additional 25% duty on products of India (9903.01.84). The 25% reciprocal rate on India ended with the other IEEPA duties on February 24.

changes.title: AGOA reauthorized through December 31, 2026
changes.detail: AGOA was renewed retroactively from September 30, 2025, when it had lapsed. AGOA (SPI D) makes the 132 dutiable Chapter 41 lines Free at the base rate for eligible sub-Saharan countries. GSP (SPI A, A+, A*) remains expired since December 31, 2020.

changes.title: Nicaragua Section 301 duty scheduled for 2027 and 2028
changes.detail: USTR set a duty on products of Nicaragua under 9903.89.01: 0% in 2026, +10% from January 1, 2027 and +15% from January 1, 2028. It reaches every Chapter 41 line but applies only to goods not entered under CAFTA-DR (SPI P).

changes.title: China fentanyl duty cut to 10%
changes.detail: The IEEPA duty on products of China and Hong Kong (9903.01.24) fell from +20% to +10%. It applied to every Chapter 41 line on top of the Section 301 duties until it ended on February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Extra 25% on products of India
changes.detail: Executive Order 14329 added 25% on Indian goods (9903.01.84), on top of the 25% reciprocal rate in force since August 7, 2025: Indian finished leather at a 5% base rate paid 55%. Ended February 7, 2026.

changes.title: Country-specific reciprocal rates; 15% floor for EU and Japanese goods
changes.detail: Executive Order 14326 replaced the 10% baseline with country rates for listed countries, for example South Africa +30% and India +25%. EU goods paid 15% in place of a lower base rate, so Italian leather paid 15%; Executive Order 14345 (signed September 4, 2025) gave Japanese goods the same 15% floor back to August 7, on top of which the 1986 40% duty still applied. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: 40% duty on products of Brazil
changes.detail: Executive Order 14323 (signed July 30, 2025) added 40% on products of Brazil (9903.01.77) on top of the 10% reciprocal duty. No Chapter 41 line was on its exemption lists, so Brazilian hides and leather paid 50% plus the base rate until February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Reciprocal tariff reaches Chapter 41
changes.detail: 10% baseline on products of all countries (9903.01.25); Canada and Mexico were excluded. No Chapter 41 line was on the reciprocal-tariff exemption list (U.S. note 2(v)(iii)). The tariff ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: China fentanyl duty raised to 20%
changes.detail: The IEEPA duty on products of China and Hong Kong (9903.01.20, then 9903.01.24) went from +10% (from February 4, 2025) to +20%, on top of the 25% or 7.5% Section 301 duty.

changes.title: Additional duties on products of Canada and Mexico
changes.detail: +25% on non-USMCA goods of Canada (9903.01.10, raised to +35% from August 1, 2025) and Mexico (9903.01.01); USMCA-qualifying goods exempt. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Countervailing duty order on leather from Argentina revoked
changes.detail: Commerce revoked the 1990 countervailing duty order on leather from Argentina (55 FR 40212) for all unliquidated entries made on or after September 20, 1991, after the Federal Circuit's Ceramica Regiomontana ruling. No antidumping or countervailing duty order has covered a Chapter 41 product since.

changes.title: Japan leather duty carried into the HTS as 9903.41.05
changes.detail: Proclamation 5911 moved the 1986 duty into the new Harmonized Tariff Schedule as heading 9903.41.05, with U.S. note 3 to Chapter 99 subchapter III making it cumulative with all other duties. Revision 21 still prints it, and U.S. note 5 does not list it among the suspended headings.

changes.title: 40% Section 301 duty on leather from Japan
changes.detail: Proclamation 5448 (signed March 16, 1986) added 40% ad valorem to bovine (including buffalo) and equine leather, and to goat, kid, sheep and lamb leather that is dyed, colored, stamped or embossed, from Japan, in response to Japan's quotas on imports of U.S. leather and footwear. It lets USTR suspend or end the duty only by a notice in the Federal Register; the only later notice (June 1986) rewrote the footwear item, not the leather item.

understandIndustry.why:
U.S. imports of Chapter 41 goods were **$450.5M in 2025**, down 2.0% from $459.5M in 2024 and well below the 2021 peak of $599.9M. **Finished bovine leather (4107) is 82% of the chapter** ($370.6M): grain splits (4107.12, $145.6M), full-grain whole hides (4107.11, $78.4M) and other whole-hide leather (4107.19, $69.3M) lead. Raw hides and skins (4101–4103) were only $10.9M.

**Italy** is the largest supplier at $166.2M (36.9%, -4.0%), almost all finished leather ($155.0M of 4107). **Brazil** rose 26.1% to $94.5M ($87.5M of finished leather and $5.3M of wet-blue and crust) even though it paid the 50% IEEPA rate from August 6. **Mexico** fell 8.0% to $62.6M, mostly finished leather ($53.3M). Germany ($21.6M), the UK ($14.6M), Argentina ($11.8M, +33.8%), South Africa ($8.6M, -39.1%) and Canada ($8.4M) follow. Imports from China fell from $10.9M in 2020 to $2.5M; Japan supplied $0.37M, nearly all finished bovine leather that pays the 1986 40% duty.

Each product has its own leader. **Wet-blue and crust cattle leather** (4104, $18.7M) comes from Brazil ($5.3M), Argentina ($4.2M), Italy ($4.0M) and Sweden ($2.0M). **Goat, pig, reptile and other leather** (4113, $24.5M) comes from South Africa ($8.6M), Colombia ($3.6M) and Pakistan ($2.3M). **Raw cattle and horse hides** (4101, $10.3M) come from Canada ($6.4M) and Mexico ($2.7M). **Composition leather and leather waste** (4115, $10.5M) come mostly from the UK ($6.5M). 2025 is the latest full year of U.S. trade data.

industryAreas.intro:
Each cell below is the base rate for that product group plus the extra duty for that country, minus any preference, from the current tariff schedule. Chapter 41 base rates are Free to 5%, so the country decides most of the total.

The 2026 Section 301 tariffs add **10% or 12.5%** on 172 of 176 lines for most suppliers; reptile and other-animal leather (4113.30, 4113.90) is exempt. **Italy** and the rest of the EU pay a flat **10%** in place of the base rate. **Brazil** pays 37.5% plus the base rate on most lines, and **China** 37.5% (leather) or 20% (raw hides). **Japan** pays 12.5% plus the 1986 duty of **40%** on bovine leather. **Mexico** is Free with USMCA; **Canada** is too, except the 14 lines with the **50% Section 338 duty**, mostly raw hides.

tariffEngineering.h1: HTS Chapter 41: Raw Hides and Skins (Other Than Furskins) and Leather — Import Documents & Ways to Lower Duty

seo.title: Importing Hides & Leather (HTS Ch. 41): APHIS, FWS & CITES Rules, Documents and Legal Ways to Lower Duty | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: The APHIS, FWS and CBP rules for each HTS Chapter 41 line — untanned hide certificates, approved establishments, CITES permits and crocodilian tags for exotic skins — and the legal ways to pay less: USMCA, the Section 301 exemptions, FTA and AGOA claims, Japan's dyed-leather rule, drawback and rulings.

tariffEngineering.intro:
For Chapter 41 the agency rules depend on how far the hide is processed and which animal it came from. **USDA APHIS** controls **untanned** hides and skins (4101–4103) to keep out foot-and-mouth disease, African swine fever and anthrax: they enter freely from disease-free regions or with a certificate or treatment (hard-dried, pickled, limed), and otherwise go to an approved establishment. Tanned, crust and finished leather of cattle, sheep, goats, pigs and horses has no APHIS or FWS gate. **FWS** rules apply to skins and leather of wild animals: reptiles, deer, ostrich and other non-domesticated species need an FWS declaration, a designated port and, for CITES species, CITES permits; crocodilian skins must carry CITES tags.

To pay less: claim **USMCA** for Canadian and Mexican goods (it does not lift Canada's 50% Section 338 duty), report the **Section 301 exemption** heading for reptile and other-animal leather and for Brazil's listed bovine lines, claim an FTA or AGOA on the 132 dutiable lines, document whether Japanese goat or sheep leather is dyed or embossed, and claim drawback on re-exported leather.

levers.title: Claim USMCA on goods from Canada or Mexico
levers.saves: The 10% Section 301 duty on 172 lines (9903.05.93 for Canada, 9903.05.94 for Mexico) and the base rate of up to 5% on the 132 dutiable lines
levers.appliesTo: All 176 lines, for goods that qualify as originating under USMCA
levers.document: A certification of origin from the importer, exporter or producer, in the importer's possession when the claim is made. It need not follow a set format.
levers.caveat: It does not lift Canada's 50% Section 338 duty on the 14 listed lines (U.S. note 51(a)): Canadian hides of 4101.20.10, 4101.20.20, 4101.50.10, 4101.50.20, 4101.90.10 and 4101.90.50, reptile skins of 4103.20.30 and upholstery leather of 4107.11.50 pay 50% with or without the claim. USMCA was not renewed at the July 1, 2026 joint review but remains in force.

levers.caveat: Note 52(b) does not lift Brazil's 25% (9903.05.01), China's 25% List 3 duty (9903.88.03) or Canada's Section 338 duty. keyTakeaways: Chapter 41 base rates are Free to 5%; the duty comes mostly from extra duties by country.
The 2026 Section 301 tariffs add 10% or 12.5% on 172 of 176 lines; only reptile and other-animal leather (4113.30, 4113.90) is exempt. Italian and other EU leather pays a flat 10%.

faqs.question: What is HTS Chapter 41?
faqs.answer: Chapter 41 of the Harmonized Tariff Schedule covers raw hides and skins (other than furskins) and leather: raw hides (4101–4103), tanned and crust leather (4104–4106), finished leather (4107, 4112, 4113), chamois, patent and metallized leather (4114) and composition leather and leather waste (4115). It has 176 tariff lines with base rates from Free to 5%. Furskins and hides with the hair on (except the kinds listed in note 1(c)) are in Chapter 43, and leather goods are in Chapter 42.

hs code for finished bovine leather
faqs.answer: Finished cowhide is heading 4107: whole hides as full grain unsplit (4107.11), grain splits (4107.12) or other (4107.19), and sides and other pieces in 4107.91, 4107.92 and 4107.99. The rate depends on use and finish: upper and lining leather of up to 28 sq ft is Free, upholstery leather 2.8%, upper and sole leather 3.3% or 5%, other leather 2.4% to 5%. Tanned or crust cowhide not further prepared is 4104 and raw cowhide 4101.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for raw hides?
faqs.answer: Raw (untanned) hides and skins are 4101 for cattle, buffalo and horses, 4102 for sheep and lambs and 4103 for other animals (reptiles 4103.20, swine 4103.30, goats, deer and others 4103.90). Whole cattle hides over 16 kg are 4101.50 and those of up to 8 kg simply dried, 10 kg dry-salted or 16 kg fresh or wet-salted are 4101.20. Hides that are not pretanned are Free; most pretanned ones pay 2.4% to 5%. Untanned hides must meet USDA APHIS rules (9 CFR 95.16).

faqs.question: What is the HS code for wet blue leather?
searchedAs: wet blue bovine leather hs code
faqs.answer: Wet-blue cattle and buffalo hides are heading 4104, in the wet state: full grains and grain splits 4104.11 and other (such as flesh splits) 4104.19. The 'wet blues' statistical lines are under 4104.11.50 and 4104.19.50 (3.3%); upper, lining, sole and buffalo leather in the wet state have their own lines (Free to 5%). Wet-blue sheepskins are 4105.10.10 (2%), goat 4106.21.10 (2.4%) and pig 4106.31.10 (4.2%). Dried crust leather is 4104.41 and 4104.49.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for goat and sheep leather?
searchedAs: hs code for goat finished leather
hs code for goat suede finished leather
faqs.answer: Finished goat and kid leather is 4113.10: 2.4% (not fancy) or 2.8% (fancy, meaning embossed, printed or decorated). Finished sheep and lamb leather is 4112.00 at 2%. Tanned or crust goat skins are 4106.21–.22 (2.4%) and sheep skins 4105 (2%); raw goat skins are 4103.90 and raw sheepskins 4102. Japanese goat and sheep leather pays 40% more if dyed, colored, stamped or embossed.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for buffalo leather?
searchedAs: hs code for buffalo finished leather
faqs.answer: Finished buffalo leather has its own lines in heading 4107 at 2.5%: 4107.11.40, 4107.12.40 and 4107.19.40 for whole hides and 4107.91.40, 4107.92.40 and 4107.99.40 for sides. Tanned or crust buffalo hides are 4104.11.30, 4104.19.30, 4104.41.30 and 4104.49.30 at 2.4%, and raw buffalo hides 4101.20.35, 4101.50.35 and 4101.90.35 (2.4%). Indian buffalo leather adds the 10% Section 301 duty.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for patent and chamois leather?
faqs.answer: Chamois leather, including combination chamois, is 4114.10 at 3.2%. Patent leather is 4114.20.30 at 2.3%, and patent laminated or metallized leather 4114.20.40 (calf and kip, 3.6%) or 4114.20.70 (1.6%). PU 'patent leather' made of plastic is not leather and is not in Chapter 41.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for bonded leather and leather scraps?
faqs.answer: Composition (bonded) leather with a basis of leather or leather fiber, in slabs, sheets or strip, is 4115.10, Free. Parings and other waste of leather or composition leather not suitable for making leather articles, and leather dust, powder and flour, are 4115.20, Free. Parings of raw hides are heading 0511. From EU countries both pay 10%, from the UK 10%, and from China 37.5% (4115.10) or 20% (4115.20).

faqs.question: What is the HS code for leather belts, wallets, bags or shoes?
faqs.answer: Not Chapter 41: that chapter covers only hides and leather as a material. Handbags, wallets and cases are heading 4202, and leather apparel, gloves and belts heading 4203, both in Chapter 42. Footwear with leather uppers is in Chapter 64 (heading 6403). Each has its own rates and extra duties.

faqs.question: Is faux or PU leather in Chapter 41?
faqs.answer: No. Chapter 41 covers only real leather, and "composition leather" (4115) must have a basis of leather or leather fiber (note 3). Faux, PU and PVC leather made of plastic or of fabric coated with plastic is classified outside Chapter 41, in the chapters for plastics or coated textile fabrics.

faqs.question: What are the U.S. tariffs on leather in 2026?
faqs.answer: The base rate (Free to 5%) plus the 2026 Section 301 duty of the country: EU leather pays a flat 10%, the UK, India, Argentina and Mexico without USMCA 10%, South Africa 12.5%. Brazil pays 37.5% plus the base rate on most lines and China 37.5% or 20%. Japanese bovine leather pays 52.5% because of a 40% duty in force since 1986. Mexican and Canadian leather is Free with USMCA, except Canada's 14 Section 338 lines at 50%. Reptile and other-animal leather is exempt from the 2026 Section 301 duties.

faqs.question: What is the tariff on leather from Italy?
faqs.answer: Italian hides and leather pay 10% in place of the base rate (9903.05.39, the EU rule of the 2026 Section 301 action), because every Chapter 41 base rate is below 10%. Italian reptile and other-animal leather (4113.30, 4113.90) pays only the base rate. Before July 24, 2026 Italian leather paid the base rate plus the 10% Section 122 surcharge, and from August 2025 to February 2026 a 15% IEEPA floor. Italian leather goods such as handbags are in Chapter 42.

faqs.question: What are the tariffs on leather from China?
searchedAs: tariffs on leather goods from china
faqs.answer: Chinese finished, crust and tanned leather (4104–4114) pays the base rate plus 25% (List 3, 9903.88.03) plus 12.5% (9903.05.31): 37.5% to 42.5%. Raw hides and leather parings pay 7.5% (List 4A) plus 12.5%. Reptile and other-animal leather pays 25%, because note 52(b) lifts only the 12.5%. USTR said on October 7, 2026 that the China lists continue during the four-year review.

faqs.question: What is the tariff on leather from India?
searchedAs: tariff on leather goods from india to usa
tariff on leather goods from india
faqs.answer: Indian hides and leather pay the base rate plus the 10% Section 301 duty (9903.05.44): 12.4% to 15% on finished cattle and buffalo leather. Reptile and other-animal leather pays only the base rate. The 2025 IEEPA duties on India (25% reciprocal plus 25% from August 27, 2025) have ended. Leather goods such as bags and wallets are in Chapter 42.

faqs.question: Do you need a CITES permit to import exotic leather?
faqs.answer: Yes for species listed under CITES, which include crocodilians, pythons and many other reptiles: the shipment needs CITES export or re-export documents (and an import permit for Appendix I species), an FWS declaration on Form 3-177 and entry through a designated port. Crocodilian skins and leather must carry a CITES tag locked through each skin (50 CFR 23.70). The tariff is low: reptile leather (4113.30) is Free and exempt from the 2026 Section 301 duties.
